title: Field-extension pullback under the abelian Galois-stalk equivalences
statement:
Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields [def-pc-field-extension], with compatible separable closures $K^s\subseteq L^s$ [def-kun-separably-closed] inside an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ containing $L^s$. Put $G_K=\operatorname{Gal}(K^s/K)$ and $G_L=\operatorname{Gal}(L^s/L)$. Write $u:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $r:\operatorname{Gal}(L^s/L)\to\operatorname{Gal}(K^s/K)$ for restriction, with the Krull topologies. Use the geometric points $p_L:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ and $p_K=u p_L$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $E_K$ and $E_L$ be the canonical equivalences of [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules], taking an abelian etale sheaf to its geometric stalk with its discrete continuous Galois action [def-exc-discrete-modules-category]. Then there is a natural additive isomorphism
$$E_L(u^{-1}F)\simeq\operatorname{Res}_r(E_K(F))$$
for every abelian sheaf $F$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Here $\operatorname{Res}_r$ leaves the underlying abelian group unchanged and makes $\tau\in\operatorname{Gal}(L^s/L)$ act as $r(\tau)$. The underlying isomorphism is the canonical stalk-pullback identification $(u^{-1}F)_{p_L}\simeq F_{p_K}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. On global sections the canonical pullback map is carried to the inclusion $M^{G_K}\to M^{G_L}$, $m\mapsto m$, for $M=E_K(F)$ with the restricted action on the right.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3); Tag 03QW (section-galois-action-stalks); Tag 04JQ (lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point); Tag 04JM (lemma-global-sections-point). The assertion packages their compatibility under an arbitrary field inclusion.

proof.text: By [lem-per-galois-restriction-image], restriction $r:G_L\to G_K$ is a well-defined continuous homomorphism for the given compatible separable closures; no algebraicity of $L/K$ is required. For a discrete continuous $G_K$-module $M$, the stabilizer of $m$ for the restricted action is $r^{-1}(\operatorname{Stab}_{G_K}(m))$, hence open. The action laws and additivity are unchanged. Equivariant homomorphisms remain equivariant after restriction, so this defines $\operatorname{Res}_r$ in [def-exc-discrete-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 0BMJ (lemma-galois-profinite), Krull topology; restriction specialization stated by lem-per-galois-restriction-image; inverse images of open stabilizers.

proof.text: Use the specified canonical natural additive isomorphism c = Etale.upperStarCompSheafFiberIso for u and p_L. Compute its germ formula by expanding its three factors: the isomorphism of geometric points transports a pointed lift to the pullback lift; the general-site sheafFiberComapIso germ formula gives the abstract pullback unit; naturality and Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app identify that unit with the constructed Etale.upperStar unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Thus c_F sends the germ of the unit-pulled section at the base-changed pointed neighbourhood to the original germ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. This proves the formula for the actual canonical comparison, not merely existence of some comparison. Represent c_F(iL(m)) by a germ using Point.toPresheafFiber_jointly_surjective; bijectivity of c_F and iL shows that every source element m is the inverse image of a pulled-back germ.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3) and the direct colimit proof; germ normalization recorded by lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ.

proof.text: For tau in G_L, apply [lem-exc-galois-automorphism-extension] over L to obtain an L-automorphism t of Omega extending tau. Restrict its scalars to K. The scalar towers and the hypothesis characterizing r show that t restricts on Ks to r(tau). Since t fixes L, Spec(t) fixes p_L. Change a pointed lift x over K by Spec(t) to x′; the pullback lift y′ is Spec(t) followed by y, as follows by the two pullback projections. Apply the supplied action-compatibility hypotheses hL and hK to these lifts. The canonical germ formula in step 2 identifies both resulting germs. Every source vector is a pulled-back germ by step 2, so d = iL followed by c followed by iK inverse is equivariant. No separate construction or choice of the canonical equivalences is needed.

source.place: Tag 03QW (section-galois-action-stalks), equation-galois-action and the subsequent surjective restriction/factorization discussion; Tag 04JQ (lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point); Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3).

proof.text: By [def-exc-discrete-modules-category], the additive equivariant bijection $c_F$ is a morphism of discrete $G_L$-modules. Its inverse is equivariant: substituting $c_F^{-1}(m)$ into $c_F(\tau x)=r(\tau)c_F(x)$ gives $\tau c_F^{-1}(m)=c_F^{-1}(r(\tau)m)$. Naturality of $c_F$ in step 2 is the same square after restriction, because restriction leaves coefficient maps unchanged. These maps consequently form the asserted natural additive isomorphism $E_L\circ u^{-1}\simeq\operatorname{Res}_r\circ E_K$, whose underlying map is precisely $c_F$.

source.place: Tags 03Q1 and 04JQ, assembly of the canonical stalk comparison as an equivariant natural isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [aux-etale-global-sections-injective] and [aux-etale-global-sections-image] over K to the supplied equivalence and stalk isomorphism. The scalar towers identify p_L followed by u with the canonical K geometric point. The actual germ map is an injective additive homomorphism with image precisely the invariant subgroup, so its codomain restriction is an additive equivalence a. Base change preserves terminal objects. Applying the same two results over L at the base-changed terminal neighbourhood gives an additive equivalence b_L. The equivariant isomorphism in step 4 transports invariants isomorphically (its inverse is equivariant too), giving b with the required germ normalization. Finally the canonical unit-on-germs formula from step 2 [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] gives b(unit(z)) = a(z) as elements of the same K module. This is the inclusion m maps to m and does not require r to be surjective.

source.place: Tag 04JM (lemma-global-sections-point), canonical terminal germ identification with invariants; Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3), for the unit germ formula.
